AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How wet should a compost heap be? (1 mark)
   A. Covered by a pool of water
   B. Damp like a squeezed sponge
   C. Dripping wet
   D. Completely dry

2. Which pupil is saving water? (1 mark)
   A. One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   B. One who leaves the tap running
   C. One who waters at midday
   D. One who pours buckets over the whole bed

3. Which stove saves more charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. A broken pot
   B. An improved jiko
   C. A stone on the ground
   D. An open fire in the wind

4. Why do we soak dry beans before cooking? (1 mark)
   A. They dry out
   B. They become bigger than the pot
   C. They become poisonous
   D. They cook in less time so less fuel is used

5. How is charcoal made? (1 mark)
   A. By burning wood slowly with little air
   B. By mixing soil and water
   C. By boiling water
   D. By drying maize

6. Why is dry grass laid lightly over a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   B. It makes seeds fly
   C. It makes the soil hard
   D. It stops seeds growing

7. Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly? (1 mark)
   A. Coconut
   B. Pawpaw tree
   C. Millet
   D. Avocado

8. Why do crowded seedlings grow badly? (1 mark)
   A. They get too much space
   B. They like company
   C. They have no roots
   D. They compete for water, light and food

9. What is transplanting? (1 mark)
   A. Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   B. Harvesting
   C. Sowing seeds directly
   D. Making compost

10. Which crop can be harvested about four to six weeks after sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Radish
   C. Banana
   D. Millet

11. Which of these fruits grows on a woody tree? (1 mark)
   A. Blackberry
   B. Passion fruit
   C. Grapes
   D. Mango

12. Why is compost mixed into the planting hole? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the hole shallow
   B. It kills the seedling
   C. It prevents growth
   D. It feeds the young plant and improves the soil

13. Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Use a picking pole and take turns
   B. Climb all trees
   C. Push each other
   D. Pull the branch down hard

14. How does eating fruit help our health? (1 mark)
   A. It gives vitamins and fibre
   B. It makes us weak
   C. It gives only sugar and nothing else
   D. It stops us drinking water

15. When should fruits be harvested? (1 mark)
   A. Before flowers appear
   B. When they are ripe
   C. While green and hard
   D. After they rot

16. Which animal browses on leaves and shoots from bushes? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Rabbit only
   D. Duck

17. Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali? (1 mark)
   A. Getting all vitamins
   B. Never feeling tired
   C. Growing very tall at once
   D. Feeling weak and getting sick often

18. Which of these animal foods is rich in protein? (1 mark)
   A. Bread
   B. Banana
   C. Cassava
   D. Fish

19. Which of these is a kitchen safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Never leave cooking food alone
   B. Play around the stove
   C. Use wet cloths
   D. Leave water near hot oil

20. About how long are eggs boiled for hard-boiled eggs? (1 mark)
   A. About 10 minutes
   B. About 5 hours
   C. One second
   D. About 10 seconds

21. What is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking without heat
   B. Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   C. Cooking in a little oil
   D. Cooking in the sun

22. Which is an advantage of boiling? (1 mark)
   A. It needs deep oil
   B. It makes food black
   C. It needs no oil
   D. It always burns food

23. Which of these foods needs a long time of boiling before it is soft enough to eat? (1 mark)
   A. Cucumber
   B. Dry beans
   C. Tomato
   D. Ripe banana

24. What is personal hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Cleaning the compound
   B. Cooking food
   C. Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   D. Washing cars

25. Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Overall
   C. Canvas shoes
   D. Dust mask

26. Which is a type of tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Cross stitch
   B. Chain stitch
   C. Even tacking
   D. Satin stitch

27. Why should you tie a knot in the thread before tacking? (1 mark)
   A. So the needle does not move
   B. To make the thread thicker
   C. So that the thread stays in the cloth
   D. To make the cloth stiffer

28. What is the use of a scarecrow shirt made with tacking? (1 mark)
   A. It waters plants
   B. It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   C. It is eaten
   D. It is a tool

29. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With a small back stitch
   B. With scissors
   C. With a very big knot
   D. By pulling the thread out

30. How long should a length of thread be for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. 1 cm
   B. As long as the room
   C. About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   D. 10 metres

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why do we dust before sweeping? (2 marks)

32. How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned? (3 marks)

33. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

34. Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment. (4 marks)

35. Explain the steps for dusting a room. (4 marks)

36. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

37. Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea. (4 marks)

38. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)

39. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

40. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

41. Why must fish be dried before shallow frying? (3 marks)

42. Design a hygiene log for one week. List five practices to record and explain how you will use it. (5 marks)

43. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

44. Give three good personal hygiene practices apart from washing hands. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Damp like a squeezed sponge
   Too dry stops rotting and too wet makes the heap smell sour.

2. A — One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   Drip watering is the most water-saving.

3. B — An improved jiko
   An improved jiko holds heat around the pot.

4. D — They cook in less time so less fuel is used
   Soaked beans soften and cook faster.

5. A — By burning wood slowly with little air
   Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

6. A — It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   Mulch protects the surface.

7. C — Millet
   Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

8. D — They compete for water, light and food
   Too many plants in a small space fight for resources.

9. A — Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   Transplanting means moving seedlings.

10. B — Radish
   Radish grows very quickly.

11. D — Mango
   Mango grows on a woody tree.

12. D — It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   Compost gives food and helps water retention.

13. A — Use a picking pole and take turns
   Use safe methods.

14. A — It gives vitamins and fibre
   Fruits protect the body and help digestion.

15. B — When they are ripe
   Ripe fruit is tastiest and has the most vitamins.

16. B — Goat
   Goats browse on shrubs.

17. D — Feeling weak and getting sick often
   One food cannot supply all nutrients.

18. D — Fish
   Fish is a protein food.

19. A — Never leave cooking food alone
   Careful supervision prevents fires.

20. A — About 10 minutes
   Ten minutes of gentle boiling makes hard eggs.

21. B — Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   Boiling uses hot water.

22. C — It needs no oil
   Boiled food is low in fat.

23. B — Dry beans
   Dry beans are hard and need long cooking.

24. C — Keeping our own bodies clean to stay healthy
   Personal hygiene is care of the body.

25. B — Overall
   An overall covers the body.

26. C — Even tacking
   Even tacking is taught in Grade 4.

27. C — So that the thread stays in the cloth
   A knot stops the thread pulling through.

28. B — It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   Tacking holds the shirt pieces together.

29. A — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

30. C — About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
   Long thread tangles.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dust falls to the floor, so sweeping afterwards removes it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dust falls, 1 mark for sweeping removes.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open windows; use a slightly damp clean cloth; dust from high to low; shake and wash the duster outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wet food makes the hot oil splash, which can burn people, so the fish should be dried with a cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for splash, 1 for burns, 1 for drying.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Practices: washed hands before meals, brushed teeth twice, bathed, clean clothes, drank safe water. Tick each day, count ticks at the end, and improve the practice with fewest ticks.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for practices and table, 2 marks for use.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, keeping nails short, wearing clean clothes, drinking safe water (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
